title: Reasoning plane — the layer the SDK does not have at all: entity graph, PPR retrieval, community summaries, as-of queries
description:
Fourth of seven plane epics (see `project-management/design/ADVANCED_MEMORY_ARCHITECTURE.md` and `project-management/AI_NATIVE_AGILE.md`).

**Invariant this plane owns:** no fact is asserted outside its valid-time interval.

This is the only plane with no existing implementation whatsoever, which makes it the highest-variance epic in the arc and the one most likely to be descoped. It is included because it is the only answer to two question classes the current SDK structurally cannot handle, and 'structurally cannot' is worth distinguishing from 'handles poorly'.

**A. Multi-hop questions are decomposition-bound, not retrieval-bound.** 'Which of the projects this user mentioned uses the database they complained about?' has no single memory whose embedding is near the query — the answer exists only as a path across two or three records. Top-k similarity search returns the wrong three memories with high confidence. Graph propagation over an entity graph fixes this: seed a restart distribution with query-matched entity nodes, run Personalized PageRank to convergence, rank memories by accumulated node mass. HippoRAG reports up to 20% improvement on multi-hop QA over strong RAG baselines at 10-30x lower cost and 6-13x lower latency than iterative retrieval (IRCoT). Cost is O(iterations x |E|) on a graph that is per-scope and therefore small — roughly 20 power iterations, cheap enough to run inline as one more RRF arm rather than as a separate query mode.

**B. Global questions are structurally unanswerable by top-k retrieval.** 'What does this user actually care about?' or 'what are the recurring themes in this agent's failures?' are query-focused summarisation over the whole corpus, not retrieval of k items from it — no value of k is correct, because the answer is a property of the distribution. GraphRAG's approach is hierarchical community detection over the entity graph plus an LLM summary per community, giving a mutually-exclusive, collectively-exhaustive cover at each level that supports divide-and-conquer summarisation. Leiden rather than Louvain, because Leiden guarantees well-connected communities and Louvain does not.

**C. Entity resolution is the unglamorous prerequisite that decides whether any of this works.** Without it 'Priyanshu', 'P. Krishnan', and `user_42` are three nodes, the graph fragments into disconnected components, PPR mass never crosses between them, and `entity_profiles` accumulates duplicates that the existing content-hash dedup cannot catch because the *content* differs. The standard blocking -> pairwise scoring -> clustering pipeline is the only way to avoid O(N^2) comparisons; the cost-controlled shape is a cascade where a cheap blocking key (normalised name, or embedding bucket) proposes candidates, a similarity function decides the clear cases, and LLM adjudication is spent only on the ambiguous band — so cost scales with the ambiguous band, not with N.

**D. As-of queries are what make EPIC-27's bi-temporal columns actually load-bearing.** Without a query path that filters `valid_from <= :t AND (valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to > :t)`, and without temporal expression extraction to produce `:t` from 'last quarter' or 'before the migration' (RTRV-7), the bi-temporal storage added in STOR-3 is inert metadata. This story is small and its value is entirely borrowed from EPIC-27 — which is the argument for doing it early rather than last.

**Two spikes gate the expensive decisions:** whether the graph projection should live in Db2 as recursive SQL or be materialised in-process — with real consequences for scope isolation, memory footprint, and whether PPR can run inline at all (GRPH-1); and at what scope size community detection starts paying for itself, since Leiden over a 40-node graph is theatre (GRPH-4).

**Scope boundary:** retrieval and summarisation over the graph. The `memory_edges` table itself is EPIC-27 (STOR-1), and edge *writing* from consolidation and reconciliation paths is STOR-2. This epic reads that graph; it does not own it.

**Depends on:** EPIC-27 STOR-1 and STOR-3, hard — no story here can start before both land. **Blocks:** nothing. This is the most deferrable plane in the arc, and if the ablation discipline in `project-management/AI_NATIVE_AGILE.md` is applied honestly it is also the most likely to be cut.
